# grepr_s3_data_warehouse_integration (Resource)

Manages a data warehouse integration that stores datasets in your S3 bucket. Grepr test-writes to the bucket when the integration is created, using the role in `assume_role_arn`. The bucket cannot change, so changing it replaces the integration.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "grepr_s3_data_warehouse_integration" "main" {
  name        = "production_s3_warehouse"
  bucket_name = "example-grepr-data"
  region      = "us-east-1"

  # Changing the bucket replaces the integration and anything built on it.
  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bucket_name` (String) S3 bucket holding the data. Changing it replaces the integration.
- `name` (String) Integration name.

### Optional

- `region` (String) AWS region of the bucket, which must be the Grepr deployment's region. The server defaults it to `us-east-1`, so set it for deployments in other regions. Removing it from the configuration keeps the current value.
- `team_ids` (Set of String) Team IDs with access. Omit to keep the current teams; an empty set clears them.

### Read-Only

- `assume_role_arn` (String) IAM role Grepr assumes to access the bucket, derived by Grepr for your organization. Grant it access to the bucket.
- `created_at` (String) Creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) Integration ID.
- `organization_id` (String) Organization owning the integration.
- `prefix` (String) Folder within the bucket where data is stored.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update timestamp.
- `version` (Number) Integration version used for optimistic locking.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import grepr_s3_data_warehouse_integration.main INTEGRATION_ID
```
